rounds.text: Arihant Capital Markets Ltd is demonstrating superior operational efficiency relative to its peers, underlined by a robust return on assets of 4.21% compared to the sector benchmark of 1.88% [E8]. This efficiency translates into a compelling return on equity of 9.94% and a return on capital employed of 12.03%, comfortably outperforming their respective sector benchmarks of 5.51% and 5.86% [E9, E10]. Momentum is firmly on the side of top-line and bottom-line expansion, evidenced by recent quarterly results showing a 33% year-on-year surge in sales and a 62% year-on-year jump in net profit [E64, E66]. Furthermore, the business is capitalising on a strong macro backdrop, with the Financial Services sector operating under a positive tailwind score of +0.77 [E73]. Technical and institutional indicators reinforce this operational strength, as the stock displays positive institutional money flow, a relative-strength rating of 80 against the Nifty 500, and a price resting comfortably above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E44, E50, E51]. Conceded: [E35, E36, E45].

The valuation is completely disconnected from fundamental reality, evidenced by a discounted cash flow model pinning intrinsic value at just Rs 48 per share against a market price of Rs 88, yielding a severe margin of safety of -81.5% [E45, E46]. Fundamental profitability metrics have severely deteriorated, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month operating margin of 37% which represents an 8 percentage point compression compared to three years prior [E30], alongside a low median return on equity of 8% over the last year [E29]. Cash generation is deeply alarming, evidenced by an operating cash flow of Rs -122 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -126 Cr in March 2026, leading to a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -3.94x [E34, E35, E36]. Balance sheet stress is mounting as borrowings expanded to Rs 271 Cr in September 2026 up from Rs 239 Cr a year earlier [E39], paired with operational bottlenecks such as exceptionally high debtors averaging 174 days [E61]. Furthermore, insiders are quietly exiting, with promoter holdings declining by 2.50 percentage points since December 2023 [E41] and down 3.96% over the last 3 years [E62]. Conceded: [E17].

While the bear highlights a low recent one-year median return on equity of 8% [E29], it ignores the robust 10-year and 5-year median ROE of 16%, proving long-term capital efficiency [E26, E27]. The bear’s concern over compressed trailing operating margins [E30] is directly countered by the most recent quarterly data showing operating margins expanding by 5 percentage points to 47% in September 2026 [E31], paired with an explicit company flag anticipating a good upcoming quarter [E59]. The bearish focus on historical DCF outputs [E45] overlooks the broader structural reality that Financial Services enjoys a strong macroeconomic tailwind with a score of +0.77 [E73], and the company is outperforming expectations with trailing twelve-month sales growth accelerating to 22% [E17] alongside a stellar +62% YoY net profit surge [E66]. Conceded: [E35, E41].

The bull points to historical 10-year and 5-year median ROE figures of 16% [E26, E27], but these long-term metrics mask a severe near-term deterioration to an 8% median ROE over the last year [E29] and an explicit screening warning regarding low ROE [E68]. While the bull highlights recent quarterly operating margin expansion [E31], it glosses over the structural multi-year compression that saw operating margins drop by 8 percentage points in the TTM period [E30] alongside an inconsistent yearly trend [E32]. The bull dismisses the DCF valuation warning [E45, E46] by citing macro tailwinds [E73] and profit surges [E66], yet the reverse DCF confirms the current price already bakes in an unrealistic 8.3% ongoing growth expectation against a base case of zero [E47], leaving an extreme overvaluation and an 82% negative margin of safety [E45, E69]. Conceded: [E17, E31, E59, E66, E73].

The bear relies on the recent ROE drop to 8% [E29] to dismiss multi-year medians of 16% [E26, E27], but ignores that the company’s broader profitability metrics—such as an ROA of 4.21%, ROE of 9.94%, and ROCE of 12.03%—all comfortably outperform their respective sector benchmarks of 1.88%, 5.51%, and 5.86% [E8, E9, E10]. While operating margins compressed over the TTM period [E30], the more recent quarterly data shows a sharp 5 percentage point expansion to 47% in September 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter [E31], aligning with expectations for a good upcoming quarter [E59]. Conceded: [E29, E30]. Furthermore, the bear's critique of the reverse DCF [E47] overlooks that the company is experiencing exceptional top-line momentum, with trailing twelve-month sales growth at 22% [E17] and recent quarterly net profit surging by 62% year-over-year [E66], supported by positive institutional money flows [E44] and a robust Financial Services sector tailwind score of +0.77 [E73]. Finally, the stock trades at an attractive EV/EBITDA of 8.15x against a sector benchmark of 13.08x [E11] and maintains a strong technical posture above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E50] with a relative-strength rating of 80 [E51].

Conceded: [E8, E9, E10, E50, E51, E73]. While the bull celebrates outperformance against sector benchmarks, it glosses over the severe deterioration in core financial reality: 5-year compounded profit growth sits at -2% [E19], and 1-year share price return is -11.6% [E52] alongside a towering annualised volatility of 53.3% [E54]. The argument that trailing sales and quarterly profit spikes override valuation risks ignores that operating cash flow collapsed to negative Rs 122 Cr and free cash flow plummeted to negative Rs 126 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E36], yielding an atrocious cash conversion of -3.94x [E34]. Furthermore, high debtors of 174 days [E61] and rising borrowings of Rs 271 Cr [E39] expose the fragility behind those headline margins, while stagnant promoter dilution of -3.96% over three years [E62] shows insiders reducing stake as the price outruns fundamentals [E56].
